title: Parsi Reform Movement
definition: A 19th-century socio-religious reform movement among the Zoroastrian community in India, primarily centered in Bombay, aimed at modernizing Parsi social customs and purging superstitious practices to align with Western education and liberal values.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the 'Westernized' segment of the Indian Renaissance, highlighting the role of urban, mercantile elites in social reform and the tension between traditional orthodoxy and modern rationalism.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Parsi Reform Movement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Western education impact on Indian elites
